biography: John Reid, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and frustration in Caterham circles, hails from the unassuming town of Brackley, Northamptonshire – a stone's throw from the heart of Formula 1. Unlike many young racers who practically emerge from the womb clutching a steering wheel, John's path was less preordained. His father, a mechanic with a penchant for tinkering, introduced him to the world of engines. Instead of go-karts, John started with rebuilding lawnmower engines, then graduated to a battered Mini Cooper his dad salvaged. This hands-on experience instilled a deep understanding of the machines he now commands. His entry into racing came unexpectedly. At a local track day, filling in for a no-show driver in a Caterham, John’s raw talent was immediately apparent. Despite his defensive driving style, he has the innate ability to extract maximum performance while protecting his position. The Caterham Supersport series provides the perfect proving ground for his talent, and he is seen as a rising star with the potential to ascend to higher echelons of motorsport. Currently, John is focused on refining his race craft and building consistency, aiming for a championship title in the coming seasons.
drivingStyle: John's driving style can be best described as 'defensive maestro.' He is not one for flashy overtakes or daring maneuvers. Instead, he focuses on precise lines, consistent lap times, and maximizing the car's potential while minimizing risk. He excels at tire management, nursing his rubber through long stints, and his defensive prowess makes him a formidable opponent to pass. He is known for his ability to place his car perfectly to defend a corner, forcing rivals to take alternative routes or risk a costly mistake. Some criticize his lack of aggression, but John believes in calculated strategy and consistent performance, preferring to secure points rather than chase glory at all costs.

rivalries.reason: A constant thorn in John's side. Isabelle's aggressive overtaking style clashes directly with John's defensive approach, leading to several on-track incidents and heated exchanges.
Marcus is John's teammate, but their contrasting approaches to car setup often lead to disagreements and a subtle, yet palpable, competition for team dominance.
Kenji is the reigning champion, and John views him as the ultimate benchmark of success in the Caterham Supersport series.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, a gift from his grandmother, on race days.
Listens to classical music (specifically Mozart) to calm his nerves before each race.
Visually inspects all four tires of his car before every session, regardless of whether they've been changed or not.
famousQuote: Sometimes, the best offense is a good defense. You can't win a race in the first corner, but you can certainly lose it.
careerHighlight: Winning the wet race at Oulton Park in 2023. He masterfully managed the treacherous conditions, defending his lead from start to finish, showcasing his exceptional car control and strategic thinking.
careerLowPoint: Spinning out on the final lap while leading at Brands Hatch in 2022. A momentary lapse in concentration cost him his first victory, a mistake he vowed never to repeat.
